title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 233 (Right of person dealing with agent personally liable)

content.overview: Section 233 provides that in cases where the agent is personally liable, a person dealing with him may hold either him or his principal, or both of them, liable. Illustration: A contracts with B to sell 100 bales of cotton and afterwards discovers B was agent for C — A may sue B or C or both for the price.
content.glance: Where agent is personally liable, third party may hold agent, principal, or both.
content.study: Where the agent is personally liable, a person dealing with the agent may hold either the agent or the principal, or both of them, liable. Illustration: A enters into a contract with B to sell him 100 bales of cotton, and afterwards discovers that B was acting as agent for C. A may sue either B or C, or both, for the price of the cotton. Current-law framing: establish personal liability of the agent; then elect among agent, principal, or both.

sections.heading: Agent personally liable
sections.body: The section applies where the agent is personally liable under the contract or the Act.

sections.heading: Third party’s election
sections.body: The person dealing with the agent may hold the agent, or the principal, or both, liable.

sections.heading: Illustration
sections.body: A sells cotton to B; later learns B was agent for C. A may sue B or C or both for the price.

provisions.title: Right of person dealing with agent personally liable

examples.title: Election against agent and principal
examples.body: A contracts with B for sale of cotton and later discovers B was C’s agent. A may sue B, C, or both for the price under the statutory illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 233 apply when the agent is not personally liable?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The section is limited to cases where the agent is personally liable.

distinctions.title: Election where agent personally liable (s. 233) vs exclusive-liability inducement (s. 234)
distinctions.left: Third party may hold agent, principal, or both
distinctions.right: Inducing exclusive-liability belief bars holding the other

misconceptions.trap: The third party must always elect only one of agent or principal.
misconceptions.correction: Section 233 expressly allows holding either or both where the agent is personally liable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 233 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Establish personal liability of the agent. II. State the third party’s election (agent, principal, or both). III. Apply the illustration if analogous. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Note the right to hold both.
